newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russian, Chechen spurn Council of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Chechen spurn Council of Europe.

text.p: Russian security boss Alexander Lebed and Chechen separatist chief of staff Aslan Maskhadov spurned a Council of Europe invitation to discuss their peace agreement on Monday.

A lower-ranking Chechen delegation came to council headquarters in Strasbourg, eastern France, for informal talks with individual parliamentarians from the 39-nation group, which seeks to promote democracy and human rights across Europe.

But Lebed and Mashkadov stayed away from a hearing on Monday on the peace deal for the breakaway Russian region which they signed on August 31. The Kremlin had blasted the invitation to Mashkadov as interference in Russian affairs.

The head of the council's parliamentary assembly, grouping delegates from all 39 member nations, issued an open-ended invitation. "We'd like to hold a meeting with Alexander Lebed and Aslan Maskhadov whenever suits them," Leni Fischer said.
"We want to back the peace agreement and its implementation," Fischer told a news conference. "Violations of human rights cannot be considered an internal affair."
She suggested November might be possible.

Swiss parliamentarian Ernst Muehlemann, who drafted a report that paved the way to Russian membership of the council in February despite misgivings about Russia's use of military force in Chechnya, presented a new report on Chechnya on Monday.

The Russian delegation to the parliamentary assembly, led by Vladimir Lukin, liberal chairman of the Russian parliament's foreign affairs committee, attended the session. He had threatened to boycott the council if Maskhadov turned up.

Lebed declined to attend after Moscow accused the organisation of interfering in internal Russian affairs and Maskhadov decided not to attend in line with an agreement with Lebed, Council officials said.
A Chechen official told the Interfax news agency in Moscow he had decided against coming because he had never received the Council's official invitation.
The French Foreign Ministry had announced on Friday that Maskhadov had been granted a visa after presenting a Russian passport at its Moscow embassy.

The Chechen delegation was led by the rebels' designated foreign minister Ruslan Chimaev, council officials said. Russia joined the Council of Europe in February only after Moscow pledged to seek a peaceful settlement in Chechnya.
